note: Hostile vectors for the R75 / R100.A2 gate. Every banned literal lives HERE, as JSON data, because .json is not an executable extension in .github/r75-policy.json — so the regression suite can exercise real banned tokens without becoming a violation itself. Fixture DATA only: the executable spec that reads this file IS scanned, as is every other test source. Cases without a legacyExit are ones whose pre-repair behaviour has not been executed, so no expectation is stated for them rather than a guessed one.

policyExpectations.note: Policy-shape expectations the spec asserts. The suppression token name lives here because naming it in executable test source would itself be an R75 violation.

legacyAlgorithm.note: The deleted pre-repair CI shell implementation, reproduced so cases can prove sensitivity to the defect being repaired. literalTokens are counted with grep -cF semantics (matching LINES, not occurrences); all counts are summed into ONE aggregate net; any line matching exemptLinePattern is discarded whole; excludeSuffixes drop test and spec sources entirely.

cases.name: same-token net-zero: an existing banned cast is only relocated
cases.why: R75 bans net ADDITIONS; a pure move must pass or the gate blocks harmless refactors.

cases.name: cross-token substitution: delete one banned token, introduce a different one
cases.why: The loophole R75 exists to close. Aggregate cross-token netting let a deletion pay for an introduction.

cases.name: cross-class swallowed-error substitution: null deleted, undefined introduced
cases.why: The three swallowed-error returns are distinct canonical tokens. One aggregated empty-catch class would net these to zero and pass — the same substitution loophole one level down.

cases.name: multiple occurrences on a single line

src/a.ts: const b = (y as any) + (z as any) + (w as any);

cases.why: grep -c counts matching LINES, so two of the three introduced casts were free.

cases.name: changed test and co-located spec sources are scanned

test/ci/thing.spec.ts: const t = v as unknown as string;
src/top.spec.ts: const s = v as unknown as string;
src/nested/deep.test.ts: const d = v as unknown as string;

cases.why: R131 records R75 being misread as src-only; the old spec/test excludes left every changed test unscanned.

cases.name: top-level source file is scanned
cases.why: Top-level files must not fall through the way a bare src/**/*.ts pathspec drops them.

cases.name: documented suppression sharing a line with another banned token

src/a.ts: // @ts-expect-error #1234 upstream typings are wrong -- const q = r as any;

cases.why: The suppression exception must affect only that directive; discarding the whole line hid every other violation on it.

cases.name: suppression with a non-empty reason is permitted

src/a.ts: // @ts-expect-error legacy SDK returns a loose shape here

cases.why: Canon requires a non-empty reason and nothing more. The old pattern demanded an issue number (#NNNN) that exists nowhere in canon, so every compliant suppression failed.

cases.name: a one-character reason is a reason
cases.why: Non-empty is the whole rule. Imposing a minimum length would be a second invented requirement.

cases.name: a non-Latin reason is a reason

src/a.ts: // @ts-expect-error 型定義が上流で誤っている

cases.why: No ASCII or alphanumeric requirement: reason validation is bounded, not a language classifier.

cases.name: suppression with no reason at all is a violation
cases.why: A bare suppression is the @ts-ignore loophole under a different name.

cases.name: suppression followed only by whitespace is a violation
cases.why: Whitespace is not a reason; this is the boundary of the non-empty rule.

cases.name: every spelling of the swallowed-error catch is detected in its own class
cases.why: 50-failures #36. The old detectors matched neither '.catch(() => null)' nor '.catch(() => {})' — the forms Prettier produces — so the canonical literals were undetectable in formatted source. Patterns normalize formatting; the return value still separates classes.
